partners.mechanism_chain: SMN1 (HGNC:10909) —DISRUPTS→ spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005654); spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005654) —LEADS_TO→ neuronal development and survival (GO:0048666); neuronal development and survival (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007353); SNRPB (HGNC:10570) —DISRUPTS→ spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005654); neuronal development and survival (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ cerebral malformations (HP:0002079); neuronal development and survival (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ mandibular hypoplasia (HP:0000226). Loss-of-function mutations in SMN1 disrupt spliceosome assembly and function, leading to motor neuron degeneration in SMA type 1. Similarly, mutations in SNRPB, also a component involved in splicing and gene regulation, disrupt neuronal development and survival, contributing to the phenotypes observed in cerebrocostomandibular syndrome. The convergence occurs at the level of the spliceosome and downstream pathways of neuronal development and survival, which are critical for both neurological and craniofacial development.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. spinal muscular atrophy, type IV  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.735)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9754678, Reactome:R-HSA-191859)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMN1 (HGNC:11117) —DISRUPTS→ SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0008134); SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0008134) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007303); SMN protein complex assembly and function (GO:0008134) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function mutations in SMN1 disrupt the assembly and function of the SMN protein complex, leading to motor neuron degeneration and muscle weakness in both SMA type 1 and SMA type IV.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in SMN1 that cause SMA type 1 with a gain-of-function mechanism, or SMA type IV with a gain-of-function mechanism, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs121918374)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting SMN protein levels or function could provide a therapeutic strategy for both severe and milder forms of spinal muscular atrophy.

---

#### 2. spinal muscular atrophy, type II  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.722)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9754678, Reactome:R-HSA-191859)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMN1 (HGNC:11117) —DISRUPTS→ Maintenance of motor neuron function (GO:0000750); Maintenance of motor neuron function (GO:0000750) —LEADS_TO→ Loss of motor neurons (HP:0003198); Maintenance of motor neuron function (GO:0000750) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Maintenance of motor neuron function (GO:0000750) —LEADS_TO→ Scoliosis (HP:0002752). Loss-of-function mutations in the SMN1 gene impair the maintenance of motor neuron function, ultimately leading to motor neuron loss, muscle weakness, and scoliosis, which are common phenotypes in both SMA Type 1 and Type II.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a distinct causal gene for either SMA Type 1 or SMA Type II, or evidence that the SMN1 gene mutations lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects rather than loss-of-function, would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism driven by SMN1 loss-of-function provides a strong basis for developing unified therapeutic strategies targeting the SMN pathway for both spinal muscular atrophy types.

Mutations in SMN1 lead to reduced levels of functional SMN protein. This deficiency impairs snRNP assembly and biogenesis, which in turn disrupts neuronal development and maintenance, ultimately manifesting as motor neuron degeneration and muscle weakness.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in SMN1 that is consistently associated with a gain-of-function mechanism or a dominant-negative effect, rather than loss-of-function, for both SMA type 1 and type III would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs743572)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared SMN1-dependent mechanism provides a unified target for therapeutic interventions aimed at increasing SMN protein levels or improving motor neuron function in both severe and milder forms of spinal muscular atrophy.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of pathogenic variants in SMN1 or RPS23 in unaffected individuals at a frequency greater than 0.01% in the general population (e.g., as observed in gnomAD) would challenge the causal link for these genes in their respective diseases. _(variant: rs121918420 (SMN1 c.661A>C) or variants in RPS23.)_
